hultsch:1876.author: Pappus of Alexandria (ed. Friedrich Hultsch)
hultsch:1876.work: Pappi Alexandrini Collectionis quae supersunt, Vol. I (Books II–V)
hultsch:1876.note: Standard critical Greek edition with parallel Latin translation and commentary for Books II (Apollonian tetrads), III (Pandrosion & Three Means), IV (Area Theorem, Arbelos & Higher Curves), and V (Honeycomb Isoperimetry & 13 Archimedean Solids).

hultsch:1877.author: Pappus of Alexandria (ed. Friedrich Hultsch)
hultsch:1877.work: Pappi Alexandrini Collectionis quae supersunt, Vol. II (Books VI–VII)
hultsch:1877.note: Standard critical Greek edition of Book VI (Little Astronomy) and Book VII (Treasury of Analysis: Preface to Hermodorus, 3/4-Line Locus, Pappus–Guldinus Centroid Theorem, Cross-Ratio VII.129, Harmonics VII.131, Hexagon Theorems VII.138–139, Focus–Directrix VII.238).

hultsch:1878.author: Pappus of Alexandria (ed. Friedrich Hultsch)
hultsch:1878.work: Pappi Alexandrini Collectionis quae supersunt, Vol. III (Book VIII & Index Graecitatis)
hultsch:1878.note: Standard critical Greek edition of Book VIII (Mechanics, Inclined Plane, Archimedes's Lever Saying, Hero's Baroulkos, Single-Opening Compass Constructions, Seven Hexagons in a Circle, and Toothed Gearwheels).

commandino:1588.author: Federico Commandino (trans.)
commandino:1588.work: Pappi Alexandrini Mathematicae Collectiones a Federico Commandino Urbinate in Latinum conversae et commentariis illustratae
commandino:1588.note: Monumental Renaissance Latin editio princeps (drawn from Vatican MS Graecus 218) through which Descartes, Guldin, Desargues, Fermat, Pascal, and Newton read Pappus before any Greek printing existed.

heath:1921.author: Sir Thomas Little Heath
heath:1921.work: A History of Greek Mathematics, Vol. II: From Aristarchus to Diophantus
heath:1921.locus: Oxford: Clarendon Press, 1921 (Ch. XIX: Pappus of Alexandria, pp. 355–439)
heath:1921.note: Comprehensive public-domain mathematical analysis of Books II–VIII of Pappus's Collection.

heath:1926.author: Sir Thomas Little Heath
heath:1926.work: The Thirteen Books of Euclid's Elements (2nd ed., 3 vols.)
heath:1926.note: Primary Euclidean commentary in geometor/euclid, citing Pappus's Synagoge across Books III, IV, V, and VI and the Treasury of Analysis.

euclid:elements.author: Euclid
euclid:elements.note: Axiomatic foundation generalized and supplemented across Pappus's Synagoge (IV.1 generalizing I.47 & VI.31; III.5–16 extending VI.13; III.54–58 complementing XIII.13–18).

euclid:data.author: Euclid
euclid:data.locus: First treatise of the Treasury of Analysis (Synagoge VII, Hultsch II pp. 636–638)
euclid:data.note: 90 propositions on magnitudes given in magnitude, ratio, species, or position; heads Pappus's 33-book curriculum of the Treasury of Analysis.

euclid:porisms.author: Euclid
euclid:porisms.locus: apud Pappum, Synagoge VII, Hultsch II pp. 648–660 & Lemmas VII.127–164 (pp. 866–918)
euclid:porisms.note: Lost three-book masterpiece of 171 propositions in 29 genera; Pappus's 38 lemmas to the Porisms include Cross-Ratio Invariance (VII.129), Harmonic Division (VII.131), and the Hexagon Theorems (VII.138–139).

euclid:surface-loci.author: Euclid
euclid:surface-loci.work: Surface Loci (Τόποι πρὸς ἐπιφανείᾳ, 2 books — lost)
euclid:surface-loci.locus: apud Pappum, Synagoge VII, Hultsch II p. 636 & Lemmas VII.235–242 (pp. 1004–1014)
euclid:surface-loci.note: Lost two-book treatise whose final Pappus lemmas (VII.238, Hultsch II p. 1008) preserve the earliest surviving proof of the Focus–Directrix eccentricity property of all three conic sections.

apollonius:conics.author: Apollonius of Perga
apollonius:conics.locus: Synagoge VII, Hultsch II pp. 672–682 & Lemmas VII.165–234 (pp. 918–1004)
apollonius:conics.note: Culmination of solid-locus geometry in the Treasury of Analysis; discussed by Pappus in connection with the Three- and Four-Line Locus and the Pappus–Guldinus Centroid Theorem.

apollonius:cutting-off-ratio.author: Apollonius of Perga
apollonius:cutting-off-ratio.work: Cutting Off of a Ratio, Cutting Off of an Area, Determinate Section, Tangencies, Inclinations & Plane Loci (12 books)
apollonius:cutting-off-ratio.locus: apud Pappum, Synagoge VII, Hultsch II pp. 636, 640–672 & Lemmas VII.1–126 (pp. 684–866)
apollonius:cutting-off-ratio.note: Six two-book Apollonian analytical treatises forming the central trunk of Pappus's Treasury of Analysis.

aristaeus:solid-loci.author: Aristaeus the Elder
aristaeus:solid-loci.work: Five Books of Solid Loci (Τόποι στερεοί, 5 books — lost)
aristaeus:solid-loci.locus: apud Pappum, Synagoge VII, Hultsch II pp. 636, 670–678
aristaeus:solid-loci.note: Pre-Apollonian treatise on conic sections connected with the Three- and Four-Line Locus problem.

archimedes:method-spirals.author: Archimedes of Syracuse
archimedes:method-spirals.work: On Spirals, Book of Lemmas (Arbelos), Semi-Regular Polyhedra & Equilibria of Planes
archimedes:method-spirals.locus: apud Pappum, Synagoge IV (pp. 208–245), V (pp. 352–358), VIII (p. 1060)
archimedes:method-spirals.note: Primary source for Pappus's arbelos circle chain (IV.14–18), spiral quadrature, complete table of all 13 Archimedean semi-regular solids (V.19), and center-of-gravity mechanics (VIII).

nicomachus:introductio.author: Nicomachus of Gerasa
nicomachus:introductio.work: Introduction to Arithmetic (Ἀριθμητικὴ Εἰσαγωγή, Book II)
nicomachus:introductio.note: Source for the ten Pythagorean and Neo-Pythagorean medieties (μεσότητες) synthesized geometrically by Pappus in Book III.

zenodorus:isoperimetric.author: Zenodorus
zenodorus:isoperimetric.work: On Isoperimetric Figures (Περὶ ἰσοπεριμέτρων σχημάτων — fragments)
zenodorus:isoperimetric.locus: apud Pappum, Synagoge V, Hultsch I pp. 308–350
zenodorus:isoperimetric.note: Hellenistic treatise on planar and spatial isoperimetric inequalities reworked and sharpened by Pappus in Book V following his Preface on the Honeycomb.

heron:mechanica.author: Hero of Alexandria
heron:mechanica.locus: apud Pappum, Synagoge VIII, Hultsch III pp. 1022–1073, 1104–1115
heron:mechanica.note: Principal Greek source for the five simple machines, toothed gear-trains, worm screw, and weight-hauling reduction preserved in Greek through Pappus Book VIII.

proclus:in-euclidem.author: Proclus Diadochus
proclus:in-euclidem.work: In Primum Euclidis Elementorum Librum Commentarii (ed. Friedlein 1873)
proclus:in-euclidem.note: Companion GEOMETOR codex preserving Pappus's symmetry proof of Elements I.5 and axiomatic remarks, while paralleling Pappus VII on geometric analysis and synthesis.

descartes:geometrie.author: René Descartes
descartes:geometrie.locus: Leiden, 1637 (Book I: The Pappus Locus Problem)
descartes:geometrie.note: Inaugurated analytic coordinate geometry specifically to solve the generalized n-line Pappus locus posed in Synagoge VII (Hultsch II pp. 676–680) via Commandino's 1588 Latin edition.

pascal:essai-coniques.author: Blaise Pascal
pascal:essai-coniques.note: Generalized Pappus's two-line Hexagon Theorem (Synagoge VII.138–139) to any smooth conic section, yielding 60 Pascal lines for six conic points.

steiner:1832.author: Jakob Steiner
steiner:1832.work: Systematische Entwickelung der Abhängigkeit geometrischer Gestalten von einander
steiner:1832.note: Established cross-ratio projectivity and proved that the six S_3 Pappus lines concur in two triples at the Steiner Star points (S_+, S_-).

hilbert:1899.author: David Hilbert
hilbert:1899.note: Demonstrated in geometor/hilbert that Pappus's Hexagon Theorem (Pascalischer Satz for two lines) is algebraically equivalent to commutativity of multiplication in the coordinate division ring.
